Why go: a small sailing catamaran on Koh Phangan's quiet coast

The Grand Voyage 42 is a 16 m sailing catamaran built in Phuket in 2020, with 3 cabins, 3 toilets and room for a group of 10 to spread out without feeling crowded. It is based at Ban Tai on Koh Phangan's south coast, which puts the island's best beaches within a short sail: the sandbar between Mae Haad and Koh Ma and the Koh Tae islets on the west side, and the cliff-backed bays of Haad Yuan, Than Sadet, Thong Nai Pan and Bottle Beach on the east. Many of the east-coast beaches have rough or no road access, so arriving by boat is the easiest way to see them.

On board you swim off the back steps, snorkel, take the SUP boards out, and use the dinghy to land on beaches the catamaran cannot reach. Twin 30 hp diesels push it along at about 7 knots when the wind drops, so the timings hold even on a still day.

Who it suits, and who should choose something else

It suits couples, families and groups of friends who want a slower, quieter day than a speedboat gives, and anyone already staying on Koh Phangan. The 3-hour sunset sail is the cheapest way onto a private sailing catamaran in this part of the Gulf.

If you are staying on Koh Samui, think twice. The boat does not come to Samui: you need a ferry or a private speedboat to Koh Phangan first, which adds cost and at least an hour each way. For a Samui departure, look at the Orana or Super King catamarans in our Koh Samui catamaran charter guide instead. Groups larger than 15 need a bigger boat; see our boat charter overview.

Good to know

  • Which coast you sail is the captain's call on the day. In the northeast monsoon (roughly November to February) the east coast takes the swell, so expect the west coast more often at that time of year.
  • November is usually the wettest month in the Samui islands. Showers often pass in an hour, but a day with strong wind can mean a change of route or date. Check the sea conditions page before you book.
  • Bottle Beach and Thong Nai Pan are a long way round from Ban Tai, so they fit best on the full day.
  • Use reef-safe sunscreen and do not stand on coral when snorkelling around Koh Ma and Koh Tae.
